title: High-Frequency Instrumentation Overhead (Observability Distortion)
pattern: A tiny, high-frequency function that executes in a few CPU cycles is instrumented with fine-grained time measurements (like `Instant::now()` or `rdtsc`) to capture telemetry for a dashboard.
why_bad: While locally improving "observability" of the function's duration, it introduces severe measurement bias. The instrumentation call itself might take 50 cycles (requiring kernel transitions or memory barriers) to measure a function that takes only 10 cycles. This severely distorts the system under test, slowing it down by 5x and masking the actual performance bottlenecks.
detection: High-frequency functions or loops that perform system-time reads or telemetry logging inside their critical loops.
counterexample: Valid when measuring large, slow operations (like a remote RPC call taking 5ms). Mark `Context-dependent`.
source: Richard L. Sites, *Understanding Software Dynamics*, Chapter 21, "The Mystery of High-Frequency Tracing" (p. 272).
